newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi says identifies 215 bodies from Haj blaze.
newsitem.headline: Saudi says identifies 215 bodies from Haj blaze.

text.p: Saudi Arabia said on Wednesday it had identified the bodies of 215 of the 343 Moslem pilgrims killed in a fire near Mecca last month, the official Saudi Press Agency said.

It quoted Saudi Health Minister Osama bin Abdul-Majid Shobokshi as saying that medical teams from his ministry used DNA tests to help identify many of the corpses that were charred beyond recognition.

Shobokshi said the identified bodies included 96 Indians, 87 Pakistanis, five each from Sudan, Egypt and Sri Lanka, two each from Yemen, Senegal and Oman and one each from China, the Ivory Coast, Bangladesh and Uzbekistan. A Saudi national and a Frenchman were also on the list of the identified bodies.
He did not identify the nationality of the remaining five victims but said more announcements would be made as the process of identification continued.
Shobokshi reiterated that the blaze, which swept through 70,000 tents and also injured more than 1,500, was an accident.

Saudi Arabia has said the fire at Mena, 11 km (seven miles) from Mecca on April 15, started when a pilgrim on the annual haj to Islam's holiest site tried to cook a meal on a gas fire inside his tent.
The tent caught fire and, partly due to strong winds, spread to other tents despite efforts by pilgrims, security services and civil defence teams.
